# mAIcro

> mAIcro is a self-hosted toolbox for personal software and rapid prototyping:
> PostgreSQL, GraphQL, documents, vectors, graphs, workflows, and AI operations
> in one local container. It speaks MCP (Model Context Protocol) natively, so
> AI agents can work with a user's data and operations as tools.

## Getting started as an AI agent

Agentic access to mAIcro is set up by the person you work for, then used by
your harness:

1. The user installs and starts mAIcro locally: https://maicro.app/get-started
2. The user generates an MCP key for their project — via the mAIcro IDE, the
   `InstanceMcpKeyGenerate` GraphQL mutation, or the CLI command
   `mcp key create --project <id>`. The key is a `projectid:secret` credential
   and must be kept out of prompts, logs, and source code.
3. The harness is configured to call the instance's MCP endpoint —
   `POST http://localhost:4321/mcp` by default — with the MCP key sent as a
   bearer credential in the `Authorization` header. In VS Code, this is an
   HTTP server entry in `.vscode/mcp.json` with the key supplied from an
   environment variable.

## Available MCP tools

- `GetSchema` — retrieve the GraphQL schema; call this first
- `DbTables` — list tables and schemas
- `DbTableAdd` — create database tables (then run the `DbReload` mutation so
  generated queries and mutations appear)
- `graphql_query` — execute read-only queries
- `graphql_mutation` — execute data modifications
- `ExecuteChain` — run chain operations (composable workflow steps)

Prefer queries before mutations, and confirm destructive operations with the
user. Everything runs on the user's machine; only AI services the user
configures send data elsewhere.
